about: The Linux native suite's engine lanes (#171, docs/doperpowers/specs/2026-10-28-own-linux-engine-design.md, The facade suites; Plan of Work M2). The two text cases require a successful method return, the marker read back exactly once and a surviving window. M1b's temporary candidate and baseline method expectations are removed. `declarations` are consumed by `node scripts/repl-parity.mjs diff <vendor-engine run> <cua-engine run> --expected scripts/repl-parity/expected/native-linux.json`: each names the vendor engine's exact declared defect (test/repl-parity/vendor-defects.json) and the exact passing cua assertion and exercise result on that case. Only those exercise results' content and isError and those case assertions are projected, and only when both sides hold exactly what they name; every other field still compares. A declaration nothing needed is itself a difference. The native baseline needs no vendor-failure waiver: its existing better-outcome rule accepts returned/survived/read-back outcomes against failures, and its Linux text cases require every cua sample to succeed while keeping Acceptance 10's engine-speed rule.
